title.value: Beyond FVD: An Enhanced Metric for Evaluating Video Generation Distribution Quality
title.justification: The title explicitly mentions the focus on advancing beyond the Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) with a new metric for video generation quality evaluation.
title.quote: B EYOND FVD: A N E NHANCED M ETRIC FOR E VALUAT - ING V IDEO G ENERATION D ISTRIBUTION Q UALITY

analysis.description: The paper critiques the limitations of the Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) as a metric for evaluating video generation quality and proposes a new metric, JEDi, leveraging features from a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy method to provide improved evaluation accuracy and efficiency.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and comparisons with other metrics on video datasets to validate the proposed JEDi metric's effectiveness.
type.quote: Our experiments on multiple open-source datasets show clear evidence that it is a superior alternative to the widely used FVD metric, requiring only 16% of the samples to reach its steady value, while increasing alignment with human evaluation by 34%, on average.

name.justification: The research is directly tied to evaluating the quality and performance of video generation methods, focusing on how distributional quality is measured.
name.quote: Recent video distance metrics focus on assessing both temporal and spatial qualities, as well as diversity, by measuring distances in distribution with respect to the real videos.

name.justification: Video generation and evaluation falls under the broader category of computer vision research.
name.quote: Video generation research has experienced a significant surge recently, yielding cutting-edge models that produce high-quality videos.

name.justification: I3D is mentioned as a key model used for extracting features in the context of evaluating video distributions using the FVD metric.
name.quote: The Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) correspond to the above equations, but the distance is applied in the space of InceptionV3 and I3D network features, respectively.

is_contributed.justification: I3D is used as a reference model for feature extraction, not developed as part of this research.
is_contributed.quote: Inflated 3D ConvNet: The Inflated 3D ConvNet (I3D) is a convolutional neural network model based on the pre-trained Inception-v1.

is_executed.justification: The research explicitly uses this model to extract features for evaluating video metrics, implying execution of the model.
is_executed.quote: FVD evaluates the FD between the generated and data distributions in the Inflated 3D ConvNet (I3D)’s feature space.

is_compared.justification: I3D features are evaluated against other models and architectures in terms of their efficacy in metric evaluations.
is_compared.quote: A comprehensive study on FVD was conducted by Ge et al. (2024), which compares Fréchet distances of features extracted by the I3D network.

referenced_paper_title.value: Quo Vadis, Action Recognition? A New Model and the Kinetics Dataset
referenced_paper_title.justification: This paper by Carreira and Zisserman discusses the I3D model, which is referenced in the research for understanding its implementation and relevance.
referenced_paper_title.quote: The Inflated 3D ConvNet (I3D) (Carreira & Zisserman, 2018) is a convolutional neural network model based on the pre-trained Inception-v1.

name.justification: V-JEPA is proposed as the new model to enhance video distribution evaluation, forming the basis for the newly introduced metric, JEDi.
name.quote: JEDi, the feature space of a V-JEPA model (V-JEPA SSv2 ) in combination with a Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) metric, is a vastly more efficient framework for evaluating distributions of generated videos than conventional methods.

is_contributed.justification: The V-JEPA model is introduced as part of the paper's contribution to improve video generation metric accuracy.
is_contributed.quote: Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture: Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA) is a self-supervised training paradigm that learns by predicting missing or masked parts of a video in an abstract representation space.

is_executed.justification: The V-JEPA model is actively used in the experiments to evaluate the JEDi metric's performance.
is_executed.quote: We employ both (1) the pre-trained variant of the model trained with the self-supervised objective, V-JEPA PT , as well as (2) a version that was fine-tuned on Something-something-v2...

is_compared.justification: The model's feature space is compared with other models like I3D and VideoMAE to demonstrate its superior alignment with human evaluations.
is_compared.quote: JEDi leverages the robust representations of a V-JEPA model, which are found to be more aligned with human evaluations compared to FVD.
